Definition: Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings
BiblicalUsage: Agag was the title of the Amalekite kings — Balaam prophesied that Israel's king would be higher than Agag, and centuries later Saul defeated Agag in battle but spared him, against God's command. Samuel had him brought out and cut him in pieces before the Lord at Gilgal, and Saul lost the kingdom for that disobedience.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Agag's story is about obedience that stops short. Saul won the battle and lost the kingdom, because partial obedience is disobedience — and the king he spared became the proof that God's commands are not suggestions.
RelatedPeople: Agag, King of Amalek; King Saul; Samuel; Balaam
